extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (primary); patent practitioners as secondary audience
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and substantive criteria for making, documenting, and responding to restriction requirements (including election, traverse, linking/generic claims, species restriction, and treatment of nonelected claims) in U.S. patent examination under MPEP guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephonic Restriction and Election Summary documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: When a telephonic restriction and election is used, the examiner must document the complete restriction requirement using the internal 'Telephonic Restriction and Election Summary' form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The form must identify the groups and species of invention(s) and, if necessary, the classification thereof; the claims corresponding to each group; the elected invention and/or species; the date of the election; the applicant or applicant representative making the election; and whether the election was with or without traverse. The form is not mailed and is used only to document the restriction requirement until an action on the merits of the elected claims is mailed. After completion, the assigned examiner will submit a C* classification picture challenge indicating the challenge resulted from an election.

rubrics_metrics.name: C* classification challenge follow-up
rubrics_metrics.description: If a C* classification challenge results in the application remaining with the original examiner, or being reassigned, the examiner must incorporate the restriction/election documentation appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the application remains, the examiner will incorporate the written restriction and election into the next Office action. If reassigned, the newly assigned examiner will document the substance of the Telephonic Restriction and Election Summary in the next Office action. If the new examiner disagrees with the original restriction requirement, differences should be resolved through chain of command (SPE or TC Director).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on telephonic restriction practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Telephone restriction practice is limited to examiners with negotiation authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners without negotiation authority must have prior approval of their supervisory patent examiner (SPE) or their reviewing primary examiner. See MPEP § 707.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of attorney requirement for telephone restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Telephone restriction practice is not permitted if a valid power of attorney has not been filed in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing representative information in an Application Data Sheet (ADS) does not constitute a power of attorney (see 37 CFR 1.76(b)(4) and MPEP § 408). Use form paragraph 8.23.03 when practitioner info is in ADS but no power of attorney of record. For appointing a power of attorney see MPEP § 402.02 et seq.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable elected invention with no rejoinder — notice of allowance handling
rubrics_metrics.description: If claims to an elected invention are allowable and no nonelected invention is eligible for rejoinder, include restriction requirement in Notice of Allowability and close prosecution of nonelected claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach the restriction requirement to PTOL-37 (Notice of Allowability), include cancellation of the nonelected claims, and a statement that prosecution is closed and a notice of allowance will be sent. Corrections of formal matters requiring applicant action should be handled under Ex parte Quayle practice using PTOL-326.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable elected invention with oral traverse — final requirement and two-month period
rubrics_metrics.description: If the elected invention is allowable in the first action and an oral traverse was noted, the examiner should make the restriction requirement final and afford applicant two months to cancel nonelected claims or take other action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include statement under MPEP § 821.01 making the restriction requirement final and give applicant two months per 37 CFR 1.144; failure to act is treated as authorization to cancel nonelected claims by examiner’s amendment and pass application to issue. Prosecution otherwise closed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check for linking/generic claims or rejoinder eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: In either traverse or no-traverse situations, examiners must determine if any allowable claims are linking and/or generic claims or if any nonelected inventions are eligible for rejoinder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat linking/generic claims specially (see MPEP § 809) and consider rejoinder rules (MPEP § 821.04).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear, detailed record of how application is restricted
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner must provide a clear and detailed record of the restriction requirement to demarcate restricted inventions for future divisional/consonance and double patenting analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The record should be detailed enough to determine whether inventions claimed in a divisional are consonant with the restriction requirement and therefore subject to double patenting prohibitions (citations: Geneva Pharms., GlaxoSmithKline). See MPEP § 804.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Species restriction specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: When restricting between species, identify the species and reasons showing they are independent/distinct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow MPEP § 809.02(a). Mention particular claim limitations and why such limitations support restriction to a particular disclosed species. Use form paragraph 8.01 or 8.02 to require election of species where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify inventions other than species by grouping claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Read all claims to determine what each claim covers and group claims directed to each separate invention with a short description of the extent of each invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the type/relationship of each group (process, subcombination, product, etc.) and indicate classification or separate status of each group (class and subclass). While every claim should be accounted for, mis-grouping or omission won't affect propriety if correct disposition is clear. See MPEP § 817.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of linking (generic) claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Generic or other linking claims should not be associated with any one of the linked inventions; they must be examined with the elected linked invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not place linking claims with a single linked invention; follow MPEP § 809 for handling linking claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness of restriction requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: When making a restriction requirement, the examiner should make every effort to have the requirement be complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If some claimed inventions are classifiable in a technology the examiner does not examine and there is doubt as to proper restriction, refer the application to an examiner who regularly examines that technology for assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outline content required for a restriction requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the prescribed outline to set forth a requirement to restrict (items A–E).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include: (A) statement that requirement is under 35 U.S.C. 121 and identify groups by Roman numerals; (1) list claims in each group and check accuracy; (3) give short description of extent of subject matter in each group and identify type (combination, subcombination, process, apparatus, product) and critical claim differences; (4) classify each group (use form paragraphs 8.08–8.11 for grouping). (B) Take into account claims not grouped and indicate disposition (linking claims, other ungrouped claims, indicate disposition e.g., improperly dependent, canceled). (C) Allegation of independence/distinctness with facts (do not merely state conclusions). (D) Provide reasons for insisting upon restriction (use form paragraphs 8.14–8.20.02). (E) Summary statement (summarize independence/distinctness and reasons; advise as to reply required; indicate effects on linking/product/evidence claims). Form paragraph 8.21 must conclude restriction requirements (except election-of-species-only situations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allegation of independence or distinctness — factual showing
rubrics_metrics.description: Point out facts demonstrating inventions are independent or distinct rather than only stating conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For various relationships, demonstrate by examiner’s suggestion or examples: (i) subcombination: subcombination disclosed as usable together but each usable alone or in other identified combinations; (ii) combination—subcombination: combination as claimed does not require subcombination AND subcombination usable alone or in other combinations; (iii) process—apparatus: process can be carried out by hand or other apparatus; (iv) process of making/apparatus for making—product made: product can be made by other processes or apparatus; (v) process of making—process of using: product used in claimed process can be made by materially different process, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons for insisting upon restriction / burden of search
rubrics_metrics.description: When asserting a serious search and/or examination burden to justify restriction, the examiner must state applicable reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Possible reasons include: separate status in the art; different classification; same classification but recognition of divergent subject matter; divergent fields of search; search required for one group not required for the other. For serious search burden, explain specific reasons such as different classes/subclasses, different search strategies or that non-prior art issues (101, 112, etc.) are relevant to one invention but not the other. Use form paragraphs 8.14–8.20.02 as appropriate; form paragraph 8.21 must be used to establish burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary statement contents
rubrics_metrics.description: The restriction requirement must include a summary statement covering independence/distinctness and effects and reply instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize (i) independence/distinctness and (ii) reasons for insisting upon restriction; include paragraph advising as to required reply; indicate effect of allowance of linking claims; indicate effect of cancellation of evidence claims; indicate effect of allowance of product claims if restriction between product and process of making/using product.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election and required reply contents
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete reply to a restriction requirement must include an election of one invention for examination and identification of claims encompassing the elected invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Election may be with or without traverse. To reserve the right to petition, the election must be made with traverse. If the reply does not distinctly and specifically point out supposed errors, the election is treated as without traverse. Traversal must be presented at time of election to be timely. If claims are added after election, applicant must indicate which claims are readable upon the elected invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traverse on non-patentable-distinctness must include evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant traverses on the ground that inventions are not patentably distinct, applicant should submit or identify evidence now of record showing the inventions to be obvious variants or clearly admit that they are so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner finds one invention unpatentable over prior art, the evidence or admission may be used in a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 103 of the other invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory use of form paragraph 8.21
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 8.21 must be added to all restriction requirements other than those containing only election of species (with or without action on the merits) or only an election by original presentation requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph establishes the burden and lists reasons for serious search/examination burden; it only needs to be used once after all restriction requirements are set out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special considerations for AIA/FITF and common-assignee double patenting
rubrics_metrics.description: Use specific AIA form paragraphs and include appropriate double patenting notices where claims are directed to same invention or not patentably distinct across commonly-assigned applications/patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use paragraphs such as 8.27.aia, 8.28.aia and include nonstatutory/provisional double patenting rejections (form paragraphs 8.31–8.37) and appropriate 102/103 paragraphs (e.g., 7.21.aia) as needed. Insert patent/application numbers and explain why claims are patentably indistinct where applicable. Include form paragraph 7.03.aia when required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint inventors — correction of inventorship
rubrics_metrics.description: When claims to a non-elected invention are canceled, correct inventorship if one or more named inventors cease to be inventors of any claim remaining in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request to correct inventorship under 37 CFR 1.48(a) must be accompanied by an application data sheet (37 CFR 1.76) identifying each inventor by legal name and the processing fee required under 37 CFR 1.17(i). Form paragraph 8.23.02 must be included in all restriction requirements for applications having joint inventors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and effect of election
rubrics_metrics.description: Election is applicant’s designation of one invention/species/group to be prosecuted in the application; examiner may make restriction if serious burden exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In reply to restriction, applicant must elect one invention for prosecution; applicant must make their own election—examiner will not do so. Election becomes fixed when the claims have received an action on their merits by the Office. After action on merits, additional properly divisible inventions may be treated as originally presented (see MPEP § 818.02(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Express election in reply and traverse requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant disagrees with restriction, they may request reconsideration and must indicate a provisional election; traverse must be a written, distinct and specific pointing out of errors under 37 CFR 1.143 and 1.111.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Election in reply may be made with or without traverse but a complete reply must include an election. A mere broad allegation is insufficient; failure to distinctly and specifically point out errors will be treated as election without traverse. Where a rejection/objection accompanies the restriction, applicant must also distinctly and specifically point out errors in the rejection or amend/argue that the objection is moot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply completeness rule
rubrics_metrics.description: A proper traverse must comply with 37 CFR 1.111(b) and be complete—specifically point out the reasons the requirement is in error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incomplete traverses result in the provisional election being treated as an election without traverse. Use form paragraph 8.25.02 to inform applicant when election treated as without traverse due to incomplete reply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traverse required to preserve right to petition
rubrics_metrics.description: To preserve the right to petition under 37 CFR 1.144, applicant must distinctly and specifically point out all errors relied upon in a timely traverse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition may be deferred until after final action or allowance of elected claims but must be filed not later than the filing date of the notice of appeal. If errors are not distinctly and specifically pointed out, the election is treated as without traverse and form paragraph 8.25.02 should be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traverse with linking claims — special rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A proper traverse with linking claims must distinctly and specifically point out errors; treatment of linking claims affects preservation of the right to petition and finality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If restriction is made final following traverse, the right to petition is preserved even if linking claims are canceled. If final restriction is contingent on nonallowability of linking claims, applicant may petition under 37 CFR 1.144 without waiting for final action on linking claims, or defer until linking claims are finally rejected (but not later than notice of appeal). An election coupled with argument that the linking claim is allowable is not a traverse (it concedes restriction proper if linking claim not allowable). If the linking claim is allowed, restriction must be withdrawn and all claims dependent from or containing the allowable linking claim must be acted upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election other than express (origination/cancellation rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Elections may be made implicitly by originally presented claims acted upon, by optional cancellation leaving claims to one invention, or by cancellation lacking an express election statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Originally presented claims acted upon determine the invention elected for restriction purposes. If applicant cancels claims to all but one invention, the remaining invention is deemed elected even without express statement. Where only generic or only linking claims were first prosecuted, later species or multiple linked inventions presented may require election per MPEP § 818.02(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Office policy on shifting elected inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants generally are not permitted to shift to claim another invention after making an election and after an Office action on the merits of the elected invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may not, as a matter of right, disaffirm/change their election after oral election and receiving Office action (37 CFR 1.142(b)), nor may they use an RCE to switch inventions as a matter of right. The examiner may permit a shift when it creates no additional burden or reduces work. Restriction in a parent does not automatically carry over to continuation/CIP/divisional unless reinstated or referred by the examiner; exceptions exist for design/CPA practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal and treatment of claims found to be to nonelected inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims found drawn to nonelected inventions are withdrawn from further consideration under 37 CFR 1.142(b) and must be clearly explained in the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner should clearly set forth reasons why withdrawn claims are not readable on the elected invention. Applicant may traverse. If final restriction is made and applicant timely traversed, applicant may petition under 37 CFR 1.144. If election results in withdrawal such that the C* classification picture is incorrect, the examiner should submit a C* classification challenge prior to action on the merits to reflect elected invention appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: After election with traverse — finalization or withdrawal
rubrics_metrics.description: If initial requirement is traversed and examiner remains of opinion restriction proper, maintain and make it final in next Office action and respond to traverse arguments; if examiner finds requirement improper, withdraw and reinstate groups as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 8.25 to make restriction final and use form paragraph 8.05 to indicate claims stand withdrawn with traverse. If restriction is withdrawn in whole or part, clearly state which groups reinstated and provide action on the merits for reinstated claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: In condition for allowance when non-elected claims withdrawn with traverse
rubrics_metrics.description: When application is otherwise in condition for allowance except for non-elected claims withdrawn with traverse, notify applicant and provide TWO MONTHS to cancel noted claims or take other action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 8.03. Failure to act in the two-month period will be treated as authorization to cancel the noted claims by examiner’s amendment and pass the case to issue. Extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) are not permitted in this situation.

rubrics_metrics.name: After election without traverse — examiner actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Where initial requirement is not traversed (expressly or via incomplete reply), examiner should act on elected claims and determine whether restriction should be withdrawn in whole or part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraphs 8.25.01 or 8.25.02 to acknowledge election without traverse and proceed to examine the elected claims; consider eligibility for rejoinder per MPEP § 821.04.
